chunks: My father narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hamman ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
God the Exalted the Sublime has not created any certitude in which there is no doubt similar to the doubt about death in which there is no certitude.
ai.seo_question: What is the paradox of death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlighting the unique ontological paradox of death: it is the only created certainty that mirrors the nature of doubt. This narration underscores the Shia theological emphasis on *yaqin* (certainty) of the Hereafter while acknowledging the human experience of *shakk* (uncertainty) regarding the moment of transition, serving as a spiritual reminder to prepare for the inevitable.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-48 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Abi Umayr, on the authority of Hamzih ibn Himran that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) said, “
God the Exalted the Sublime has not created any certitude in which there is no doubt similar to the doubt about death in which there is no certitude.”
